callTitle: Renewable energy financing mechanism technology specific
descriptionByte:
Expected Impact:

The projects must contribute to the realisation of additional renewable energy capacity across the EU in a cost-effective way and the timely delivery of renewable energy statistics to the participating Member States. The beneficiaries will be expected to report renewable energy production on an annual basis.

Objective:

The objective is to contribute to the clean energy transition and the Clean Industrial Deal objectives including the goals and objectives of the Paris Agreement, the 2030 climate and energy targets and 2050 carbon neutrality objective. The call shall also contribute to the implementation of Directive 2018/2001 as amended by Directive (EU) 2023/2413 and of the Governance Regulation which sets out an indicative trajectory from 2021 to 2030 for each Member State’s contribution to the Union’s renewables target, with three reference points to be reached in 2022, 2025 and 2027. In this sense, Member States can use the RENEWFM to fill a gap towards the indicative Union trajectory which is the key objective of this call.

More specifically, this topic targets ground mounted solar PV with co-located BESS and ground mounted solar PV projects. Solar PV is a well-established and low-cost renewable energy technology aimed at high reliability in terms of deploying fully operational renewable electricity (RES-E) capacities and generation volumes and thus assumes effective and quick project realization from awarded project applicants. Likewise, the costs of battery energy storage systems are rapidly falling, and the co-location of such equipment with a renewable energy production facility entails significant benefits for both the generation installation and the electrical system. By sharing the same grid access point, synergies between the generation and storage systems can be maximised to improve generation profile, optimise grid capacity utilisation, save infrastructure costs, and ultimately enable the integration of higher shares of renewable energy.

Scope:

The following activities aiming at the deployment of new renewable energy capacities can be funded:

RES technology and location:

  • ground mounted solar PV projects with co-located BESS located in Bulgaria, in the districts of Pernik, Kyustendik or Stara Zagora.
  • ground mounted solar PV projects located in Finland (except the region of Åland).

A project is considered as a standalone renewable energy project if it is connected to the electricity grid (or to the off-taker, in case of off-grid projects) via a single connection point.

Specific conditions per RES technology and per hosting MS apply and are detailed in Section 2 of the Call document.

title: RFCS-2026-01-AM Coal Accompanying measures
callTitle: RFCS-2026
descriptionByte:
Expected Impact:

Accompanying measures are expected to ensure a balanced representation, within the consortium, of relevant academia, research centres, industry and/or industry associations, including just transition actors. They should also involve stakeholders required for the just transition of coal regions. In addition, accompanying measures may provide suggestions for policy initiatives that contribute to the digital, green and circular transformation of the coal communities, in line with the European Green Deal.

Objective:

Proposals submitted under this topic should relate to one or more of the RFCS objectives for coal, as set out in Council Decision 2008/376/EC.

Scope:

Accompanying measures aim to promote the use of knowledge gained or the organisation of dedicated workshops or conferences in connection with projects or priorities of the RFCS.

title: RFCS-2026-01-PDP Coal Pilot and demonstration projects
callTitle: RFCS-2026
descriptionByte:
Expected Impact:

Each proposal must include an assessment of the expected industrial, economic, social and environmental benefits (Article 26 of Council Decision 2008/376/EC).

Objective:

Proposals submitted under this topic should relate to one or more of the RFCS objectives for coal as set out in Council Decision 2008/376/EC.

Scope:

Pilot projects target the construction, operation and development of installations on an appropriate scale. Demonstration projects cover the construction and/or operation of industrial-scale installations.Both pilot and demonstration projects aim to bridge the gap between research and innovation. Pilot and demonstration activities are expected to start at TRL 4-5 and achieve TRL 7-8 by the end of the project.

title: RFCS-2026-Steel-Big Tickets under the steel and metals action plan dual-use
callTitle: RFCS-2026-Steel-Big Tickets under the steel and metals action plan dual-use
descriptionByte:
Expected Impact:

1. Project results are expected to contribute to all of the following outcomes:

  • quantify the CO2 reduction and other positive environmental effects achieved in the steel sector;
  • make it technically and economically feasible for novel technologies and processes to produce products of at least the same quality as that achieved using current industrial processes, as demonstrated and validated on a suitable scale;
  • demonstrate, where relevant, positive health and safety effects of the technology and/or the approach pursued;
  • outline a scalable deployment plan for the technology, supported by a viable business case;
  • disseminate results widely and contribute to the development of skills and the creation/conversion of jobs.

2. Project results are expected to contribute to the following impacts:

  • progress towards the goals of the European Green Deal, in line with the European Commission policy guidelines applicable to the steel industry for the full decarbonisation of the steel sector;
  • support innovation and competitiveness in the steel sector as a strategic element for strengthening the European industrial base and autonomy.

Proposals relating to dual-use applications must demonstrate, in the impact section of the application form, how the proposed research and innovation activities will benefit both the civil and the defence sectors.

Objective:

Proposals should address one of the following objectives:

1. New, sustainable and low-carbon steelmaking and finishing processes (Article 8).

  • Proposals should address objectives listed in Article 8 of Council Decision 2008/376/EC.

2. Advanced steel grades and applications (Article 9).

  • Proposals should address objectives listed under Article 9 of Council Decision 2008/376/EC.

Proposals addressing dual-use applications should aim to develop innovative products and processes relevant to both the civil and the defence markets in the steel sector.

Scope:

  • Applicants may submit proposals for either pilot or demonstration projects (see Articles 15 and 16 of Council Decision 2008/376/EC).
  • Proposals must relate to the application of innovative technologies related to at least one of the objectives.
  • Proposals submitted under this specific call are expected to achieve TRL 5-8 by the end of the project.
  • Proposed activities are expected to start at TRL 3-4 and achieve at least TRL 5 (Technology validated in a relevant environment) or TRL 6 (Technology demonstrated in a relevant environment).
  • Proposals must include an exploitation strategy outlining the possible industrial integration of the outcomes of the project (including the pilot/demonstrators) and a preliminary assessment of their economic viability.
  • Targeted improvements (relative to existing installations or, for new projects, to the relevant ETS benchmark) must be clearly quantified and demonstrated using energy system and material balance assessments (including emissions), which must be clearly defined by the applicants.
  • Proposals addressing dual-use applications must demonstrate, in the excellence section of the application form, how the proposed research and innovation activities are linked to civil and defence aspects.
  • Proposals should not contain EU classified information, as defined in the Council Decision on the security rules for protecting EU classified information
  • The European Commission’s steel and metals action plan acknowledges that the European steel sector is vital for the EU’s economic security and defence capabilities. The action plan stresses that ensuring a stable and resilient supply chain for steel and other key metals is critical for strengthening the European Defence Technological and Industrial Base, ensuring the EU’s preparedness and internal security, meeting EU defence and aerospace needs, and ensuring technological sovereignty. In this context, the utmost priority should be given to strengthening the EU’s strategic autonomy in steel production capacities for defence applications. For these reasons, and in line with Article 136(3) of the Financial Regulation, to protect the security of the European Union and its Member States, participation in this call is limited to legal entities established in EU Member States. In addition, participants (beneficiaries, affiliated entities, associated partners, and subcontractors) must not be directly or indirectly controlled by any country other than an EU Member State or by a legal entity established in such a country.

results.content: RENEW-BOOSTER EUROCLUSTER CALL N°2 FOR FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO THIRD PARTIES

beneficiaryAdministration:
More detailed information about the call may be found here

To apply, please complete the submission form on EU SURVEY

Applications may be modified as long as the deadline is respected: you will be able to save and come back later on EU Survey. The platform will be automatically closed at the date and time announced, that is November 30th, 2026, at 5:00 pm CET. Applicants will receive an e-mail confirming that their application has been well uploaded on the platform. Shall you not receive the confirmation e-mail, please contact Benjamin Schmidt at bes@energycluster.dk and copy your local contact point. SMEs applying as a consortium should fill in one proposal. One of the involved SMEs will act as a “coordinator” and will be responsible for the submission of the application.

RENEW BOOSTER Eurocluster innovation mechanism will support projects in the "challenges" call and projects in the "open" call, at least 3 SMEs and up to €60,000 euros per SME.


Evaluation Process and Criteria

All eligible applications will be evaluated by evaluators against the criteria defined in the RENEW-BOOSTER Call Text: Excellence, Impact and Quality and efficiency of implementation. Each criterion is scored from 0 to 10, with a minimum threshold of 6/10 per criterion.

Indicative timeline:

  1. Call deadline: 30 November 2026 (17:00 CET)
  2. Evaluation: December 2026
  3. Results communication: Mid-January 2027
  4. Contract signature: End-January 2027

For full details on the evaluation methodology, scoring, thresholds, and tie-breaking rules, please see the call text


Proposals will be eligible only if all the following conditions are met:

  1. Applicants must be established in one of the following eligible countries: EU-27 + countries participating in the SMP/COSME strand.
  2. Applicants must be SMEs according to the European Union definition of SMEs: the formal definition is available here and the SME self-assessment questionnaire is available here.
  3. Applications must address either the Challenge Call or the Open Call, as described in the Call Text. For applications submitted under the Challenge Call, detailed descriptions of the challenges can be found here or in the EUSurvey submission form.
  4. Applications must be written in English (applications partially written in another language are not eligible) and must not exceed the maximum number of characters stated in each text box of the pre-defined template available on the submission platform;
  5. Applications must be submitted through EU Survey
  6. SMEs may apply individually to the Challenge Call (Strand A). For the Open Call (Strand B), SMEs may apply either individually or as part of a consortium of up to 3 SMEs.
  7. Each SME may submit a maximum of one application under Strand A and one application under Strand B, whether applying individually or as part of a consortium. Applications submitted under both strands must address different activities and must not result in double funding. Any SME submitting more than one application to the same strand will be automatically disqualified.
  8. No annexes can be submitted other than the ones demanded on the EU Survey platform.
  9. Every applicant organisation needs to be registered on the EU F&T Portal and have a 9-digit Participant Identification Code (PIC). Please find all information PIC number.
  10. This call requires private co-funding. Further information can be found here on page 5-7.
  11. At least 10% of funded SMEs should come from countries or regions other than those represented in the consortium; Denmark, Norway, Poland, France, Bulgaria and Spain.
description:
The two calls will be structured through two distinct funding strands. It is reminded that the cumulative maximum FSTP support per SME under the whole set of RENEW-BOOSTER calls is EUR 60,000. An SME may submit a maximum of one application per strand, whether applying individually or as part of a consortium. Consequently, an SME may submit one application under Strand A and one application under Strand B, provided that the proposed activities are distinct and no double funding occurs.

Strand A (Challenge-driven) follows a two-step process linked to predefined industrial challenges. In Step 1, up to three SMEs per challenge receive €10,000 (with minimum 20% private co-funding) to develop and validate a proof of concept (TRL 6-7). After evaluation and a final pitch, one SME per challenge advances to Step 2 and receives €50,000 (with minimum 40% co-funding) to further develop and scale the solution (TRL 8–9).

Strand B (Open Call) follows a single-stage selection process. SMEs apply bottom-up and can request up to €10,000, €30,000, or €60,000 depending on project maturity, with increasing private co-funding requirements. Projects run up to six months.

callTitle: RENEW-BOOSTER EUROCLUSTER CALL N°2 FOR FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO THIRD PARTIES
furtherInformation:
The RENEW-BOOSTER project aims at driving innovation and industrialization in three critical sectors that are vital for Europe’s green transition and energy security: Photovoltaics (PV), Offshore Wind Energy, and the associated Energy Networks. At the core of RENEW-BOOSTER is the Accelerator, providing tailored support for SMEs to identify opportunities and develop solutions, strengthening their role in the renewable energy value chain and enhancing resilience.

The project aligns with Europe’s strategic priorities, including reducing critical raw material dependency (Critical Raw Materials Act), advancing climate goals (Green Deal), and supporting re-industrialization (Net Zero Industry Act). RENEW-BOOSTER aims to empower SMEs and accelerate Europe’s twin green and digital transitions.

We reserve the right not to award all available funds or to redistribute them between the different calls, depending on the proposals received and the results of the evaluation.

For answers to frequently asked questions, please visit our FAQ.
